To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the L1-estimator of a moving average time series model is asymptotically equivalent to a linear combination of the L1-estimate of the mean, and the L1- estimate of a linear function of the observations.

the limiting distribution of the L 1-estimate of the moving average model is a mixture of the standard normal distribution and the distribution of the maximum of independent and identically distributed random variables.
the asymptotic behavior of L 1 -estimators for q th -order moving average models under more general condition on the distribution function around zero is derived.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following three aspects.

the following three problems: (i) the asymptotic distribution of L 0-estimators in MA(q) models with q ≥ 2 under more general conditions; (ii) the asymptotic behavior of L 1 -estimators in MA(1) models under more general assumptions; and (iii) the asymptotic normality of the L 1-estimate in MA(q) with q ≥ 1 under more general conditions.

the following two problems: (1) the asymptotic distribution of L 0-estimators for MA(q) models under the condition that F (0) = 0; (2) the asymptotic distributions of L 1, 2-estimators for the MA(q) model with F (0) ≠ 0.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for qth order MA(q) models, L 1- and L p-estimators (p>1) have the same asymptotic distribution.
the asymptotic distribution of L 0,1-estimators in MA(q) models with a finite variance and a symmetric distribution function is the same as in the case of MA(1) models.

, under the conditions given, the limiting distribution of the L 1-estimate for MA(q) models is a normal random variable, and the limiting variance of the estimate is the reciprocal of the sum of the squares of the coefficients of the moving average.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, under the conditions of the paper, L 1-estimate of MA(q) model is asymptotically normal.
the limiting distribution of the L 1-estimate is a mixture of the normal distribution and a point mass at the zero.
, for a wide class of distribution functions near zero, the asymptotic distribution of the L 1-estimate is a normal random variable.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the limiting distribution is a weighted sum of a normal distribution with the same mean and variance as the classical L 1-estimate and a degenerate distribution with a mass point at the true value of the parameter.
the asymptotic distribution of the estimators depends not only on the order of the moving average process, but also on the tail behavior of the error term.

the limiting distribution of the L 1-estimate is the same as that of the L 2-estimate, but the limiting distribution is not normal, but rather the distribution of the sum of two independent random variables with different distributions, one of which is a normal random variable.
